title: Opening habits: one checked failure each
outcomes: Gives one checked position where taking the centre fails, one where moving a piece again is right, and one where castling is not the move
Says which condition made each habit fail: an attacked square, a loose piece, a pawn that only a trade can leave loose
Recognises a position where none of the three habits fails

steps.text: **When the opening habits fail: reasons and conditions** showed that a habit gives way to a threat. Here each habit gets its own checked failure. Start with the centre. A centre pawn is only as good as the square it lands on, so before you push, count the enemy pieces that attack that square and your own pieces that defend it. This is a *rule of thumb*: count first, then push.

Second habit: do not move a piece twice before the others are out. The reason is time, and time is worth little when a piece of yours is loose (attacked and not defended). If the piece that has already moved is the one in danger, moving it again is the development that counts. *Rule of thumb:* a loose piece comes before a new piece.

Third habit: castle early. Castling puts the king away, but it does not defend anything else. Before you castle, ask what a trade could leave loose. A pawn defended only by a piece that can be traded off is the usual case. In the next pair, a position where the d6 pawn defends e5 is set against one where only the c6 knight does.

steps.title: Castle now?
steps.prompt: Black wants to castle in both positions. Predict whether castling is sound in each, then check.

steps.caption: The position from the failing half of the pair. Step through what castling allows.

line.say: White trades the bishop for the knight.
The e5 pawn has no defender and White takes it.

steps.text: Conditions, one line each. *Centre:* fails when the square is attacked more often than it is defended. *Moving twice:* right when the piece that moved is the one attacked. *Castling:* fails when it leaves a pawn or piece loose after a trade. All three are *rules of thumb*. The next positions do not say which one applies, and in one of them none fails.

steps.prompt: Pick one of your recent games. Which habit did you follow in the first ten moves, and what did you check about the position before you followed it?
